report.source_text: Chest computed tomography showed emphysematous changes bilaterally with multiple prominent pulmonary bullae bilaterally (blue arrows), the largest in the anterior left upper lobe and posterior right lower lobes (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3). There were multiple associated regions of bronchiectasis (red arrowheads) and bronchial wall thickening. There was also dilatation of the pulmonary vasculature (red arrows), which should measure <3 cm just proximal to the bifurcation of the left and right pulmonary arteries (Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 3).

clinician.final_diagnosis: unique case of COPD bullous emphysema with superimposed pneumonia in a woman of African origin with no hereditary predispositions or social risk factors
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old woman presented with progressively worsening productive cough, fatigue, shortness of breath, and palpitations. Physical examination revealed mild respiratory distress, bilateral diffuse rales and rhonchi, and significant exertional desaturation requiring supplemental oxygen. Chest CT imaging demonstrated bilateral emphysematous changes with multiple prominent pulmonary bullae and bronchiectasis, consistent with COPD bullous emphysema. Respiratory cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida albicans, confirming superimposed pneumonia, treated initially with ceftriaxone and azithromycin then broad-spectrum antibiotics including vancomycin and cefepime. Treatment also included supplemental oxygen, methylprednisolone, and bronchodilators. Spirometry obtained two weeks post-admission showed severe airflow limitation (FEV1 23%, FEV1/FVC 65%) confirming COPD diagnosis. The patient’s symptoms improved with treatment.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Chest CT shows bilateral emphysematous changes with multiple prominent pulmonary bullae and bronchiectasis
Respiratory cultures positive for Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Candida albicans confirming pneumonia
Treatment included antibiotics, supplemental oxygen, corticosteroids, and bronchodilators leading to symptom improvement
Spirometry shows severe airflow limitation consistent with COPD (FEV1 23%, FEV1/FVC 65%)
